originality.rationale: The novel assertion is the sharp, universal-angle-variance stability and its optimality, not the already-published polygon chord density or local formula. Published formulas provide the statistic, but their inspected statements do not contain or logically directly state the sharp uniform inequality, which requires a global differential inequality plus polygonal realizability of an extremizing sequence. Substantial abstract-only historical source risk remains.
residual_risks: Gates 1987 full text could contain a related sharp extremal statement; it was not accessible after open-access search and an authorized institutional attempt.
Old chord-integration literature might contain an unindexed inequality stated in different angular coordinates.

The identical sharp 1/6 factor and extremal pattern in a prior boundary-pair statistic could be viewed as a method-level generalization; the two actual probability statistics and their functions are not implication-equivalent.

value.rationale: The initial frequency of short Crofton chords is a natural measurable inverse-geometric statistic. For arbitrary convex polygons, the sharp scale-free inequality gives quantitative control of the squared variance of exterior turns from this single number, uniform in side count and polygon scale. Exact equality and attainability of the optimal constant distinguish this from an angle-function substitution alone. Length information remains irrecoverable, appropriately limiting the claim.
